description.en: Discover patterns with unsupervised learning — K-Means and DBSCAN, choosing K with the elbow method, and cluster evaluation.

story_variants.en:
## Clustering: Finding Groups in Unlabelled Data

**Clustering** is an **unsupervised** learning task — you have data but no labels. The algorithm finds natural groups (clusters) on its own.

### K-Means Clustering

K-Means divides data into **K clusters** by iteratively:
1. Assigning each point to the nearest centroid
2. Moving centroids to the mean of assigned points
3. Repeating until stable

```python
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs
import numpy as np

# Synthetic data with 4 natural clusters
X, _ = make_blobs(n_samples=300, centers=4, random_state=42)

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=42, n_init=10)
kmeans.fit(X)

labels = kmeans.labels_          # cluster id per sample
centroids = kmeans.cluster_centers_  # centroid coordinates
print(labels[:10])  # e.g. [1 0 3 2 1 0 0 3 ...]
```

### Choosing K: The Elbow Method

```python
inertias = []
for k in range(1, 10):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
    km.fit(X)
    inertias.append(km.inertia_)

# Plot inertias and look for the 'elbow' — the k where
# improvement starts to diminish
```

### DBSCAN: Density-Based Clustering

Unlike K-Means, **DBSCAN** does not need K upfront. It finds clusters of arbitrary shape and marks noise as `-1`:

```python
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN

db = DBSCAN(eps=0.5, min_samples=5)
db.fit(X)
labels_db = db.labels_  # -1 = noise
```

### K-Means vs DBSCAN

| Aspect | K-Means | DBSCAN |
|--------|---------|--------|
| K required | Yes | No |
| Cluster shape | Spherical only | Arbitrary |
| Handles noise | No | Yes (labels as -1) |
| Scalability | Fast | Slower for large data |

> **Key Insight:** K-Means works best when clusters are roughly spherical and similar in size. DBSCAN shines when clusters have irregular shapes or when you need to automatically detect outliers (noise points).

## குழுப்படுத்தல்: சேராத தரவில் குழுக்களைக் கண்டறிதல்

**குழுப்படுத்தல்** என்பது ஒரு **கண்காணிக்கப்படாத** (unsupervised) கற்றல் பணி — நீங்களுக்கு தரவு உள்ளது, ஆனால் சிட்டைகள் (labels) இல்லை. அல்கோரிதம் தன்னிச்சையாக இயற்கையான குழுக்களை (clusters) கண்டறிகிறது.

### K-Means குழுப்படுத்தல்

K-Means தரவை **K குழுக்களாக** பிரிக்கிறது, இதற்காக மீண்டும் மீண்டும்:
1. ஒவ்வொரு புள்ளியையும் அருகிலுள்ள மையப்புள்ளிக்கு (centroid) ஒதுக்குதல்
2. ஒதுக்கப்பட்ட புள்ளிகளின் சராசரியை எடுத்து மையப்புள்ளிகளை நகர்த்துதல்
3. நிலையானதாக இருக்கும் வரை மீண்டும் செய்தல்

```python
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs
import numpy as np

# Synthetic data with 4 natural clusters
X, _ = make_blobs(n_samples=300, centers=4, random_state=42)

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=42, n_init=10)
kmeans.fit(X)

labels = kmeans.labels_          # cluster id per sample
centroids = kmeans.cluster_centers_  # centroid coordinates
print(labels[:10])  # e.g. [1 0 3 2 1 0 0 3 ...]
```

### க் தேர்வு செய்வது: மூக்கு முறை (Elbow Method)

```python
inertias = []
for k in range(1, 10):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
    km.fit(X)
    inertias.append(km.inertia_)

# Plot inertias and look for the 'elbow' — the k where
# improvement starts to diminish
```

### DBSCAN: அடர்த்தி அடிப்படையிலான குழுப்படுத்தல்

K-Means போலல்லாமல், **DBSCAN** முன்பே K-ஐ தேவைப்படுத்துவதில்லை. இது எந்தவொரு வடிவமைப்பிலும் உள்ள குழுக்களைக் கண்டறியும் மற்றும் சதுரங்கத்தை `-1` என குறிக்கிறது:

```python
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN

db = DBSCAN(eps=0.5, min_samples=5)
db.fit(X)
labels_db = db.labels_  # -1 = noise
```

### K-Means vs DBSCAN

| அம்சம் | K-Means | DBSCAN |
|--------|---------|--------|
| K தேவை | ஆம் | இல்லை |
| குழு வடிவம் | கோள வடிவம் மட்டும் | எந்தவொரு வடிவமும் |
| சதவீதத்தைக் கையாளுதல் | இல்லை | ஆம் (-1 என சிட்டையிடுதல்) |
| அளவிடக்கூடிய தன்மை | வேகமாக | பெரிய தரவுக்கு மிஞ்சும் வேகம் குறைவு |

> **முக்கிய உணர்வு:** K-Means சிறப்பாக செயல்படுகிறது என்றால், குழுக்கள் பொதுவாக கோள வடிவத்தில் இருக்கும் மற்றும் அளவில் ஒத்திருக்கும். DBSCAN சிறப்பாக செயல்படுகிறது என்றால், குழுக்கள் அசாதாரண வடிவங்களைக் கொண்டிருக்கும் அல்லது நீங்கள் தானியக்கமாக வெளிப்படையான புள்ளிகளை (noise points) கண்டறிய வேண்டும் போது.

## గుంపులుః గుర్తించని డేటా లో సమూహాలను కనుగొనడం

**క్లస్టర్** అనేది** పర్యవేక్షణ లేని** అభ్యాస పని.

### K-మీన్స్ క్లాస్టింగ్

K-Means ఐటరియటివ్గా డేటాను **K క్లస్టర్లుగా** విభజిస్తుందిః
1. ప్రతి పాయింట్ను సమీప కేంద్రకమునకు కేటాయించడం
2. కేటాయించిన పాయింట్ల మధ్యస్థానికి సెంట్రాయిడ్లను తరలించడం
3. స్థిరంగా ఉండే వరకు పునరావృతం

```python
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs
import numpy as np

# Synthetic data with 4 natural clusters
X, _ = make_blobs(n_samples=300, centers=4, random_state=42)

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=42, n_init=10)
kmeans.fit(X)

labels = kmeans.labels_          # cluster id per sample
centroids = kmeans.cluster_centers_  # centroid coordinates
print(labels[:10])  # e.g. [1 0 3 2 1 0 0 3 ...]
```

### K ను ఎంచుకోవడంః ఎల్బౌ పద్ధతి

```python
inertias = []
for k in range(1, 10):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
    km.fit(X)
    inertias.append(km.inertia_)

# Plot inertias and look for the 'elbow' — the k where
# improvement starts to diminish
```

### DBSCAN: సాంద్రత ఆధారిత సమూహాలు

K-Means కాకుండా, **DBSCAN** కి ముందుగా K అవసరం లేదు. ఇది వాంఛనీయ ఆకారం గల సమూహాలను కనుగొంటుంది మరియు శబ్దాన్ని `-1` గా గుర్తించిందిః

```python
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN

db = DBSCAN(eps=0.5, min_samples=5)
db.fit(X)
labels_db = db.labels_  # -1 = noise
```

### K-Means vs DBSCAN

 అస్పెక్ట్  కె-మీన్స్  DBSCAN 
|--------|---------|--------|
 K అవసరం  అవును  లేదు 
 గుంపు ఆకారం  గోళీ  స్వచ్ఛంద 
 శబ్దం  లేదు  అవును 
 స్కేలబిలిటీ  వేగంగా  పెద్ద డేటా కోసం నెమ్మదిగా 

> ** కీ ఇన్సైట్ః** K-మీన్స్ గుంపులు సుమారు గోళాకారంగా మరియు పరిమాణంలో సమానంగా ఉన్నప్పుడు ఉత్తమంగా పనిచేస్తుంది. గుంపులు అక్రమ ఆకృతులను కలిగి ఉన్నప్పుడు లేదా మీరు స్వయంచాలకంగా అసాధారణమైన (శబ్దం పాయింట్లు) గుర్తించాల్సిన అవసరం ఉన్నప్పుడు DBSCAN ప్రకాశిస్తుంది.

## ഗ്രൂപ്പിംഗ്ഃ ലേബൽ ചെയ്യാത്ത ഡാറ്റയിൽ ഗ്രൂപ്പുകൾ കണ്ടെത്തുക

**ക്ലസ്റ്ററിംഗ്** എന്നത്**അശ്രദ്ധ* പഠന ചുമതലയാണ്. നിങ്ങൾക്ക് ഡാറ്റയുണ്ട്, പക്ഷേ ലേബലുകൾ ഇല്ല. അൽഗോരിതം സ്വാഭാവിക ഗ്രൂപ്പുകൾ (ഗ്രൂപ്പുകൾ) സ്വന്തമായി കണ്ടെത്തുന്നു.

### കെ-എൻഡ് ക്ലസ്റ്ററിംഗ്

K-Means ഡാറ്റയെ **K ക്ലസ്റ്ററുകളായി** ഇറ്ററേറ്റീവ് ആയി വിഭജിക്കുന്നുഃ
1. ഓരോ പോയിന്റും ഏറ്റവും അടുത്തുള്ള സെൻട്രോയിഡിലേക്ക് നിയോഗിക്കുക
2. സെന്റ്രോയിഡുകൾ നിശ്ചയിച്ചിരിക്കുന്ന പോയിന്റുകളുടെ മധ്യത്തിലേക്ക് നീക്കുക
3. സ്ഥിരതയുള്ളതുവരെ ആവർത്തിക്കുക

```python
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs
import numpy as np

# Synthetic data with 4 natural clusters
X, _ = make_blobs(n_samples=300, centers=4, random_state=42)

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=42, n_init=10)
kmeans.fit(X)

labels = kmeans.labels_          # cluster id per sample
centroids = kmeans.cluster_centers_  # centroid coordinates
print(labels[:10])  # e.g. [1 0 3 2 1 0 0 3 ...]
```

### K തിരഞ്ഞെടുക്കുകഃ എൽബോ രീതി

```python
inertias = []
for k in range(1, 10):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
    km.fit(X)
    inertias.append(km.inertia_)

# Plot inertias and look for the 'elbow' — the k where
# improvement starts to diminish
```

### ഡിബിഎസ്കാൻഃ സാന്ദ്രത അടിസ്ഥാനമാക്കിയുള്ള കൂട്ടിച്ചേർക്കൽ

K-Means- ൽ നിന്ന് വ്യത്യസ്തമായി, **DBSCAN- ന് മുൻകൂർ K ആവശ്യമില്ല. അത് സ്വമേധയാ രൂപമുള്ള ക്ലസ്റ്ററുകൾ കണ്ടെത്തുകയും ശബ്ദം `-1` എന്ന് അടയാളപ്പെടുത്തുകയും ചെയ്യുന്നുഃ

```python
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN

db = DBSCAN(eps=0.5, min_samples=5)
db.fit(X)
labels_db = db.labels_  # -1 = noise
```

### കെ-മീൻസ് vs ഡിബിഎസ്കാൻ

∙∙∙കി-എന്നാൽ ∙∙∙ഡിബിഎസ്കാൻ
|--------|---------|--------|
∙ കെ ആവശ്യമുണ്ട് ∙ അതെ ∙ ഇല്ല ∙
∙∙∙കോമ്പ് ആകൃതി ∙∙കോമ്പ് ആകൃതി മാത്രം ∙∙
∙∙∙അതെ, അതെ, ∙
∙ സ്കേലബിളിറ്റി ∙ വേഗതയുള്ള ∙ വലിയ ഡാറ്റയ്ക്ക് വേഗത കുറവാണ് ∙

> ** കീ ഇൻസൈറ്റ്ഃ** ക്ലോസ്റ്ററുകൾ ഏകദേശം ഗോളവും വലുപ്പവും സമാനമാണെങ്കിൽ K-മീൻ മികച്ച രീതിയിൽ പ്രവർത്തിക്കുന്നു. ക്ലോസ്റ്ററുകൾക്ക് അക്രമകരമായ രൂപങ്ങളുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ ഓട്ടോമാറ്റിക് വേർതിരിവ് (ശബ്ദചിഹ്നങ്ങൾ) കണ്ടെത്തേണ്ടിവരുമ്പോൾ DBSCAN തിളങ്ങുന്നു.

## Clustering: recherche de groupes dans les données non étiquetées

**Le regroupement** est une tâche d'apprentissage non supervisée** vous avez des données mais pas d'étiquettes.

### K-Means Clustering

K-Means divise les données en **K clusters** par des méthodes itératives:
1. Allouer chaque point au centre-point le plus proche
2. Mettre les centroides en moyenne des points attribués
3. Répétez jusqu'à ce que le niveau de l'eau soit stable

```python
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs
import numpy as np

# Synthetic data with 4 natural clusters
X, _ = make_blobs(n_samples=300, centers=4, random_state=42)

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=42, n_init=10)
kmeans.fit(X)

labels = kmeans.labels_          # cluster id per sample
centroids = kmeans.cluster_centers_  # centroid coordinates
print(labels[:10])  # e.g. [1 0 3 2 1 0 0 3 ...]
```

### Choisir K: la méthode du coude

```python
inertias = []
for k in range(1, 10):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
    km.fit(X)
    inertias.append(km.inertia_)

# Plot inertias and look for the 'elbow' — the k where
# improvement starts to diminish
```

### DBSCAN: Clustering basé sur la densité

Contrairement à K-Means, **DBSCAN** ne nécessite pas K à l'avance. Il trouve des grappes de forme arbitraire et marque le bruit comme `-1`:

```python
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN

db = DBSCAN(eps=0.5, min_samples=5)
db.fit(X)
labels_db = db.labels_  # -1 = noise
```

### K-Means contre DBSCAN

Je suis un homme qui a une vision de la vie.
|--------|---------|--------|
Je veux que tu me donnes un coup de main.
Je suis un homme qui a une vie de rêve.
Je suis un homme qui a des problèmes avec les gens.
Je suis un peu plus rapide que vous.

> ** Key Insight:** K-Means fonctionne mieux lorsque les amas sont à peu près sphériques et de taille similaire. DBSCAN brille lorsque les amas ont des formes irrégulières ou lorsque vous devez détecter automatiquement des points de bruit.

## Clustering: Encontrar grupos en datos no etiquetados

**Clustering** es una tarea de aprendizaje** no supervisada**  tienes datos pero no etiquetas. El algoritmo encuentra grupos naturales (clusters) por sí mismo.

### K-Means Clustering

K-Means divide los datos en ** K clusters** por medio de la siguiente manera:
1. Assignar cada punto al centroide más cercano
2. Movimiento de los centroides a la media de los puntos asignados
3. Repetición hasta que se establezca

```python
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs
import numpy as np

# Synthetic data with 4 natural clusters
X, _ = make_blobs(n_samples=300, centers=4, random_state=42)

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=42, n_init=10)
kmeans.fit(X)

labels = kmeans.labels_          # cluster id per sample
centroids = kmeans.cluster_centers_  # centroid coordinates
print(labels[:10])  # e.g. [1 0 3 2 1 0 0 3 ...]
```

### Elegir K: El método del codo

```python
inertias = []
for k in range(1, 10):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
    km.fit(X)
    inertias.append(km.inertia_)

# Plot inertias and look for the 'elbow' — the k where
# improvement starts to diminish
```

### DBSCAN: Clustering basado en la densidad

A diferencia de K-Means, **DBSCAN** no necesita K por adelantado. encuentra grupos de forma arbitraria y marca el ruido como `-1`:

```python
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN

db = DBSCAN(eps=0.5, min_samples=5)
db.fit(X)
labels_db = db.labels_  # -1 = noise
```

### K-Means vs DBSCAN

# Aspecto # K-Means # DBSCAN
|--------|---------|--------|
Se requiere K Sí No
♪ Forma de grupo ♪ Solo esférica ♪ Arbitraria ♪
# Se encarga del ruido # No # Sí #
 Escalabilidad  Rápido  Lento para grandes datos 

> **Key Insight:** K-Means funciona mejor cuando los racimos son aproximadamente esféricos y de tamaño similar. DBSCAN brilla cuando los racimos tienen formas irregulares o cuando se necesita detectar automáticamente los valores de diferencia (puntos de ruido).

## Clusterizzazione: Trovare gruppi in dati non etichettati

**Clustering** è un compito di apprendimento non supervisionato** si hanno dati ma non ci sono etichette.

### K-Means Clustering

K-Means divide i dati in **K cluster** iterativamente:
1. Assegnazione di ogni punto al centroide più vicino
2. Movimento dei centriodi alla media dei punti assegnati
3. Ripetizione fino a stabilizzazione

```python
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs
import numpy as np

# Synthetic data with 4 natural clusters
X, _ = make_blobs(n_samples=300, centers=4, random_state=42)

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=42, n_init=10)
kmeans.fit(X)

labels = kmeans.labels_          # cluster id per sample
centroids = kmeans.cluster_centers_  # centroid coordinates
print(labels[:10])  # e.g. [1 0 3 2 1 0 0 3 ...]
```

### Scegliere K: il metodo del gomito

```python
inertias = []
for k in range(1, 10):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
    km.fit(X)
    inertias.append(km.inertia_)

# Plot inertias and look for the 'elbow' — the k where
# improvement starts to diminish
```

### DBSCAN: Clustering basato sulla densità

A differenza di K-Means, **DBSCAN** non ha bisogno di K in anticipo. Trova gruppi di forma arbitraria e segna il rumore come `-1`:

```python
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN

db = DBSCAN(eps=0.5, min_samples=5)
db.fit(X)
labels_db = db.labels_  # -1 = noise
```

### K-Means vs DBSCAN

# Aspetto # # K-Means #
|--------|---------|--------|
# # E' necessario # # Sì # # No #
♬ Forma di ammasso ♬ Solo sferica ♬ Arbitrario ♬
# Gestisce il rumore # No, si. #
♬ Scalabilità ♬ Rapido ♬ Più lento per i grandi dati ♬

> **Key Insight:** K-Means funziona meglio quando i cluster sono approssimativamente sferici e di dimensioni simili.

## 그룹: 표기되지 않은 데이터에서 그룹을 찾아내는 방법

**집단**은 ** 감독되지 않은** 학습 작업입니다.

### K-미디어 그룹화

K-Means는 데이터를 반복적으로 **K 클러스터**로 나눕니다:
1. 각 점들을 가장 가까운 중위점으로 할당하는 것
2. 중앙형의 이동이 지정된 점의 평균으로
3. 안정될 때까지 반복

```python
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs
import numpy as np

# Synthetic data with 4 natural clusters
X, _ = make_blobs(n_samples=300, centers=4, random_state=42)

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=42, n_init=10)
kmeans.fit(X)

labels = kmeans.labels_          # cluster id per sample
centroids = kmeans.cluster_centers_  # centroid coordinates
print(labels[:10])  # e.g. [1 0 3 2 1 0 0 3 ...]
```

### K 를 선택: 팔꿈치 방법

```python
inertias = []
for k in range(1, 10):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
    km.fit(X)
    inertias.append(km.inertia_)

# Plot inertias and look for the 'elbow' — the k where
# improvement starts to diminish
```

### DBSCAN: 밀도 기반 클러스터링

K-Means과 달리 **DBSCAN**는 K를 미리 필요로 하지 않습니다. 임의의 모양의 클러스터를 발견하고 `-1`로 소음을 표시합니다.

```python
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN

db = DBSCAN(eps=0.5, min_samples=5)
db.fit(X)
labels_db = db.labels_  # -1 = noise
```

### K-Means vs DBSCAN

          
|--------|---------|--------|
 K가 필요해요
 크기가 크죠. 은 크기가 크죠.
          
 масшта비얼리티  빠른 慢慢  빅 데이터

> **키 인사이트:** K-매치는 클러스터가 대략 구형적이고 크기가 비슷할 때 가장 잘 작동합니다. DBSCAN은 클러스터가 불규칙한 모양을 가지고 있거나 자동적으로 비정상 (소음점) 을 감지해야 할 때 빛납니다.

under_the_hood.summary: scikit-learn's KMeans runs the assign-and-average loop from several starts and keeps the run with the lowest inertia, while DBSCAN labels points by density in one pass; both just return integer cluster labels with no meaning beyond 'same group'.

steps.title: KMeans.fit runs several starts
steps.body: KMeans(n_clusters=4, n_init=10) runs the whole algorithm 10 times from different k-means++ starting centroids. Each run alternates assigning points to the nearest centroid and moving centroids to the mean until they stop moving. The run with the lowest inertia_ wins and supplies cluster_centers_ and labels_.

nodes.label: keep the run with lowest inertia

steps.title: Label numbers are arbitrary
steps.body: Cluster 0 in one run might be cluster 2 in another; the numbers only mean 'these points belong together'. To compare a clustering with known labels use adjusted_rand_score, which ignores how clusters are numbered, rather than accuracy.

steps.title: predict means nearest centre
steps.body: After fitting, kmeans.predict(new_points) just computes the distance from each new point to the 4 stored centres and returns the nearest one's label; no centres move. DBSCAN has no predict method because its clusters are defined by the training points' density, so you use fit_predict on the data you have.

steps.title: The elbow loop
steps.body: Fitting KMeans for K = 1 to 8 and recording inertia_ gives a falling curve, because more centres always sit closer to the points. On make_blobs data with 4 centres the curve drops steeply until K = 4 and then flattens; that bend is the elbow.

props.caption: Typical inertia pattern for data with 4 blobs

steps.title: Silhouette checks separation
steps.body: silhouette_score(X, labels) computes, for every point, a = mean distance to its own cluster and b = mean distance to the nearest other cluster, then averages (b - a) / max(a, b). It needs all pairwise distances, so it gets slow beyond tens of thousands of points; sample_size lets it score a random subset.

under_the_hood.takeaway: In scikit-learn, clustering is fit, then read labels_. KMeans keeps its best of n_init runs and can predict new points; DBSCAN cannot. Judge results with silhouette or, when you have true labels, adjusted Rand, never with raw label numbers.
